stories.headline: Bears' Caleb Williams questionable after 3 days of practice
stories.summary: Williams said there are several hurdles to clear before he would be able to face the Falcons on Sunday.
stories.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Caleb Williams was officially listed as questionable on the Chicago Bears' final injury report ahead of their Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons.

Williams was a full participant during the Bears' Wednesday walk-through and practice sessions on Thursday and Friday. The quarterback said he had to go through "a bunch of medical protocols" before being cleared by team trainers, which could happen before the team leaves for Atlanta.

"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "He looked good [Thursday] for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. Part of the plan, and he's on track right now."

Williams missed three straight games while recovering from a hamstring injury sustained during the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. On Thursday, he took issue with the reporting around his injury, for which he claimed that "nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been."

Johnson did not sense that his quarterback was frustrated with anything other than not being able to play.

"I honestly, I didn't feel any frustration from him," Johnson said. "He was in this little bit of a no-man's land, 'Hey, what do I what do with myself? I've never been in this situation. I've never been in the training room this much. I've never been second or third fiddle in the quarterback room ever in my life.' Just like, 'I just need a little guidance on how I can best help and serve.'

"He's a captain, he wants to do that desperately. How can I help us win in this different setting? I don't know that I felt frustration, other than an eagerness to get back out there and help the guys on the field."

While Williams' status is questionable, the Bears will be without running back Kyle Monangai for a second straight game. Monangai did not practice this week while recovering from thumb and toe injuries, the latter of which he visited a specialist for last week.

"It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said. "So, it's still week to week and as far as I know, he's trending in the right direction."

Chicago will also be down three starters on defense amid defensive end Montez Sweat's two-game suspension for violating the PED policy and injuries that are sidelining linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) in Week 6.

stories.headline: It's as easy as ever to manage your fantasy hockey team in just minutes a day
stories.summary: Managing your fantasy hockey lineup is easier than you think with this easy-to-follow daily routine.
stories.body:
When it comes to typical fantasy enthusiasts hesitant about diving into the NHL game specifically, I often hear the same refrain: It takes too much time. This message is usually being relayed from participants accustomed to the NFL version, who appreciate only having to care about games mostly on Sundays, with the added Thursday and Monday tentpole games.

I get it. The NHL is an everyday league. But that doesn't mean you need to carve out large slices of your busy life to ice a competitive fantasy hockey squad, each and every night. Minutes per day is all that's required. I timed it. Plus it's fun. Everyone is busy with work, school, kids, and other real-life responsibilities. If nothing else, taking a few minutes most days can also provide a brief moment of fantasy-related Zen.

To provide the necessary help along the way, ESPN's Fantasy Hockey department is here to deliver analysis and advice in easily digestible bites. The following guide provides a day-by-day weekly plan of how to manage your roster, in all forms of leagues that allow you to make daily adjustments, be it adding or dropping, starting or sitting, or considering trades.

More: Rankings | Most added/dropped | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | Weekly picks | Sign up

Monday: The most important day (7-8 minutes)
First, quickly set your fantasy table for the week by adjusting your lineup day by day. This way, even if life takes over, you don't have skaters or goalies sitting on your bench when they could be active otherwise. Then give your roster a more thorough sussing-over. Is anyone hurt? Underperforming? If an underachieving contributor is still seeing heavy minutes and filling a prominent role, leave it be for now.

The adds/drops (+/-) column is also helpful here. If throngs of fantasy managers are abandoning a certain character, it isn't a coincidence. Once those less useful are identified or hurt, toss them on IR, or dump them altogether, and peruse our Monday weekly pickups guide for potential replacements. If pressed for time, a quick skim of names will suffice. We like to provide the reasoning for each pickup, but trust us that we've done the research.

If you play on the ESPN Fantasy app, you can see the recommended weekly pickups right on your home screen.

In H2H competition, it's also worth zoning in on our favorite streamers of the week. These are players who are both checking off the fantasy boxes while also competing when most others are not. The NHL is a Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday league. Skaters and goalies who are on the ice on more so-called off days can provide just enough extra juice to make the difference between weekly victory and defeat. Every fantasy roster should have at least one slot for potential streamers, depending on your weekly or season-long transaction limits.

Pro Tip: The ESPN Fantasy game provides a Quick Lineup button in the upper right-hand corner of your roster page. This handy-dandy tool makes lineup adjustments "based on player active status, highest projected points, highest average points and player rating (for category and Roto leagues)". Have zero time to set your lineup? Let the robots handle matters! Obviously, this device is most useful closest to puck drop when a player's status is as relevant as possible.

While many leagues allow for shuffling players in and out everyday, others include a cap on weekly transactions or limit games played per slot to avoid having to prioritize quantity over quality. Make sure to plan accordingly in step with those limits.

Tuesday/Wednesday: Speedy skim (4-5 minutes)
Quickly survey your roster with an eye to injuries or other issues. Again, relying on ESPN's Quick Lineup feature can be advantageous, particularly close to puck drop.

Thursday: Column Catchup (7-8 minutes)

For those willing to invest a little extra time, Thursday's deeper-dive material offers the chance to seize an extra advantage over your less well-read competition. Rotating through a variety of fantasy-relevant material, like how to hack the schedule, what to really expect from this year's crop of rookies, a closer look at the fallout from certain significant injuries, or the fantasy consequences related to stories making general NHL headlines, Sean Allen and yours truly endeavor to provide analysis beyond that shallowly provided by the +/- column. Even if you learn one valuable tidbit, this is time well spent. Otherwise, like any other day of the week, give your lineup a quick scan for red-inked signs of disaster.

If you play on the ESPN Fantasy app, you will get a push notification every time a new advice column is published, as well as when a player in your lineup is ruled out.

Friday: Rankings review (6-7 minutes)
After giving your roster the usual once-over, check out Allen's top-250 rankings. If one of your competitors is dropping like a stone that particular week, there's undoubtedly a good explanation. Figure out whether they deserve more time or a return to the wire and, in case of the latter, snatch someone who's on the obvious rise.

Heading into the weekend, it's time to start scrutinizing your box score in Category Leagues. If you're steamrolling your competition in one category -- hits, blocked shots, power-play points etc. -- but lagging in another, that should help decide who to activate and/or bench on Saturday when far more players are competing than not.

The weekend: Lineup management (7-8 minutes)
Even following a reasonably successful week, one jam-packed Saturday can rapidly submarine your fantasy scorecard altogether. Which is why it's extra vital to make the wisest decisions possible on who to start/sit, based on trending performance, current role, and strength of matchup. If one of your non-star forwards is facing the hottest hand in net, behind one of the league's stingiest defense, bench him. (You're never benching a healthy Connor McDavid. Connor Bedard has not yet earned that distinction.)

Hopefully you're sitting pretty by the time Sunday roles around, when it's time to pay extra attention to specific stats in Category Leagues. Flush in hits? Consider showing that specialist streamer the fantasy door, while ushering in a needed power-play performer or such.

That's it, that's all. An average of seven minutes per day and anyone with a solid enough roster can remain competitive throughout the 2026-27 fantasy season. We're just getting started; there's still plenty of time to sign up and join in the fun. New leagues start every Monday.

Download the ESPN Fantasy Sports app and have every player right at your fingertips. Available on the App Store and Google Play.

stories.headline: Spanish team challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's NBA eligibility
stories.summary: A Spanish basketball team is challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, saying he is still under contract with the club.
stories.body:
Spanish club Basket Zaragoza is challenging Oklahoma City Thunder rookie lottery pick Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, stating that he remains under contract with the team for the 2026-27 season, a contention disputed by the Thunder.

In a statement released Friday, Basket Zaragoza said it has not received an official request from the Thunder for Mara's international transfer and would formally oppose the transfer if a request is made.

"Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a Thunder spokesperson said Friday.

Basket Zaragoza said its position was formally communicated to FIBA, the Spanish Basketball Federation, the NBA and the Thunder after Oklahoma City selected Mara with the No. 12 pick in June's draft.

Mara, a native of Zaragoza, left the club in 2023 to go to UCLA. However, FIBA regulations do not require an official international transfer for NCAA participation, and Basket Zaragoza's stance is that Mara's contract with the club was not terminated during his college tenure. After two seasons at UCLA, the 7-foot-3 Mara transferred to Michigan, where he started on last season's national championship team before entering the draft.

The 21-year-old Mara had an outstanding preseason for Oklahoma City, averaging 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks while shooting 78.8% from the floor in 23.3 minutes per game. He is projected to be part of a deep center rotation for the Thunder, who use 7-footers Isaiah Hartenstein and Chet Holmgren in the starting lineup and bring Jaylin Williams off the bench.

stories.headline: Miami coach unbothered by Messi getting award in Spain 2 days before MLS game
stories.summary: Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive a prestigious award before rejoining the club for an MLS game two days later.
stories.body:
Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, before rejoining the club for the match against the New York Red Bulls two days later.

Messi is due to attend the ceremony in Oviedo on Oct. 22 ahead of Miami's MLS game against the Red Bulls in Harrison, New Jersey.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami back to winning ways, as Nashville chase history

- Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'

But González said he had no concerns about Messi's travel schedule ahead of the game.

"Yes, he does have this event [in Oviedo], and I love that he will assume it in this way. The whole club agrees that he should be there because it is a terribly important award, not just for him but for his family," González told reporters on Friday.

"Then, of course, I will count on him for the game [against the New York Red Bulls]. Leo has the possibility, not an advantage, and I said it the other day after the match, I want him to be good.

"He needs this. He'll be there, then I will have him at the game so I'm not worried about that at all."

The Princess of Asturias Award recognizes individuals and institutions for notable achievements in fields like literature, social sciences, scientific and technical research, international cooperation and sports.

Messi became the first individual football player to be given the honor by the jury, which consists of several members -- including president of the foundation Teresa Perales -- when it was announced in June.

"The truth is that for me it is a great pride to be able to receive this recognition because of the importance it has and for the fact that it is recognized not only for what I do on the pitch but also off the pitch," Messi said when the award was announced.

"I am very happy, and very grateful. I wanted to let you know and send a big hug to everyone. Thank you and see you soon."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table and secured its place in the 2026 MLS playoffs on Wednesday.

Messi leads MLS' Golden Boot race with 23 goals, four goals ahead of nearest challenger Petar Musa of FC Dallas.

Ahead of the game at the Red Bulls, Miami will visit Atlanta United FC on Saturday.

stories.headline: How Dodgers' three-peat hopes ended with NLCS loss to Brewers
stories.summary: The Dodgers' October came to a screeching halt with a sweep at the hands of the Brewers. What's next in Los Angeles?
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Enduring regret often lingers from postseason defeat, those nagging thoughts of what could have been, what should have been, what might have been. The 2025 Toronto Blue Jays are haunted by such memories from last fall's World Series.

But there is none of that for the 2026 Los Angeles Dodgers, following the last night of baseball in their quest for a third straight World Series title. The Milwaukee Brewers wrecked them in a one-sided series that presents carte blanche for whatever changes the L.A. front office deems necessary, from upgrading the team's speed and defense to a reassessment of the deference granted to the ambitions of the sport's most popular star, Shohei Ohtani.

The question that hovered over this entire major league season was whether anyone could beat the Dodgers. Now, after dominating the National League Championship Series, the Brewers appear to be the new standard.

"We got outplayed in all facets," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Those guys played flawless. Defensively they pitched better than we did, they hit better than we did, they slugged more than we did. You've got to sometimes just tip your cap."

The Milwaukee Brewers outscored the Dodgers 21-9 and outhomered them 7-1. Whenever L.A. scored, the Brewers counterpunched immediately.

There was some evident Dodgers angst occasionally strewn during the game. Like when Ohtani clubbed his home run in the second inning, his first in almost two months. He shed his typically polite decorum and showed another side of Shohei, shouting and pumping his arms at teammates in the home dugout and waving emphatically to the fans in left field, with his left hand and then his right, and unleashing a primal scream when he got back in the dugout. "I think it was a lot of pent-up anger, frustration," Roberts said. "It was the best ball he hit in probably two, three months, and it was a big hit."

Max Muncy struck out to end the sixth and disgustedly dumped no fewer than seven pieces of equipment: his bat, followed by his helmet, followed by various pieces of protective gear. But after the last out, after the Brewers' bullpen stifled them again, there didn't seem to be a lot of tears in the Dodger clubhouse. Miguel Rojas -- a big brother to this group, Mookie Betts said -- announced to the group that he is retiring, as expected. Freddie Freeman spoke. Betts offered some words, and so did Roberts. Just lots of perspective.

After reporters entered the room, Ohtani said through his interpreter, "The Brewers were overall strong and a very good team, and it really exposed some of the parts of me as a player, and got to give some credit to that."

The failed attempt at back-to-back-to-back championships, Mookie Betts said, "was hard, man. It's hard. You know, you go back to where we started in Korea a couple years ago. It's been like nonstop since. It's been a grind, but I mean it's part of the game. Part of life."

Kiké Hernandez was asked if these Dodgers were like dinosaurs hit by a meteor -- the implication that they were made extinct.

"Obviously we had a lot of expectations," he said. "We fell short. We had a good run, but here we are. I don't know what's going to happen with me personally, moving forward for next year. But this team is well positioned to keep winning and keep competing deep into October. So not only is this locker room very talented, but there's a lot of guys knocking on the door in the minor league system that can be really impactful players. So the organization is in good hands. We just, we fell short."

Such perspective comes with experience -- and the Dodgers have lots of experience. Freddie Freeman is 37, Muncy is 36, Betts is 34. Ohtani is 32. Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Edwin Diaz, Teoscar Hernandez, Will Smith, Tommy Edman are all in their 30s. Many are on the downslope of accomplished careers.

Before the game, Freeman smiled when asked about the age of the Dodgers' roster. "We do know we have an older team," he said. "That doesn't mean we're old and we're playing bad because we're old. We're just not playing that great, in my mind."

"I don't feel old. So hopefully when you watch us play tonight, you can say we don't look old and we win the game."

But the Dodgers didn't win, and they did look older and slower than Milwaukee. While the Brewers outfielders seemingly covered acres of outfield, making play after play, the Dodgers slogged. Milwaukee shortstop Cooper Pratt is 22 years old and doesn't have much experience or perspective, and in the ninth inning, he backhanded a ball and whipped a missile to first base for an out. Back in 2020, when they won their first title of this era, the Dodgers were widely lauded as a dynamic, athletic team. Now, even Dodgers fans seemed worn down: There were rows of empty upper-deck seats in the left- and right-field corners; the Game 4 attendance of 49,104 was less than the team's regular-season average.

There is clearly a need for the Dodgers to regain that dynamism of 2020, and it won't happen without change. Andrew Friedman, the head of baseball operations, must decide with his staff whether it can succeed with Hernandez locked into one spot in the outfield, and how much more Muncy can give. Freeman is eligible for free agency after next season. It must decide whether to invest the hundreds of millions of dollars that will be required to retain Skubal, who thrived in his time with the Dodgers but is now a free agent, with his 30th birthday next month.

Complicating all of these choices is baseball's looming labor war. Nobody knows for sure what the economic system will be and whether there will be more restrictions aimed at curbing the Dodgers' financial advantages over other teams.

So much of the Dodgers' plans revolve around Ohtani, generally viewed as the best player of this generation -- maybe all generations -- and he will go into the offseason under thick clouds of doubt. Is his persistent left knee trouble this year something that Ohtani, as a right-handed pitcher, can overcome? Can he be a full-time pitcher again? Is it better for Ohtani and the Dodgers that he commits himself solely to hitting? Could he play in the field or is he a DH only, and how might that impact Freeman, a first baseman, or Josue De Paula, the team's best hitting prospect?

Since Ohtani was a teenager, he has been driven to be a two-way player, to be the best hitter and the best pitcher, and the Dodgers have largely deferred to him in this, with success. But this year, his efforts to pitch led to injuries to his knee and biceps, which in turn affected his offense. He struggled terribly at the plate in the last games of the regular season and the playoffs before his home run in Game 4. If his name wasn't Ohtani, if he didn't have the bank of MVPs and acclaim, he might've been a candidate to be left off the Dodgers' postseason roster.

He tried to make it work. It didn't.

After Game 4, Ohtani was asked about what's next for him as a two-way player, and whether that's something he'll continue, and he responded through an interpreter that he was "not quite satisfied with how things shaped up on the pitching side at the end of the year. This year, I haven't pitched, and I haven't pitched in the postseason. You know, I haven't been able to really come to grips in terms of what I've learned overall this season. It's something that I'm going to kind of go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training program, and see what I can come up with for next season."

The Dodgers have a lot of really good players, a strong farm system, more resources than anyone. But they reached a fork in their journey Thursday night, with uncertainty ahead.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

stories.headline: F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?
stories.summary: The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.
stories.body:
The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.

Most drivers secured short-term deals to survive the regulation shift, leaving the grid wide open for the following year. With only a handful of drivers locked into long-term contracts almost every seat on the grid is up for grabs.

Here is our early look at what the future holds for the current Formula 1 lineup.

McLaren

Lando Norris - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2030

Prior to the start of the 2024 F1 season Norris agreed to an "extended multi-year contract beyond 2025."

The reigning champion has now signed a new contract with McLaren until at least 2030. The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multi-year" extension beyond 2030.

Oscar Piastri - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Ahead of the first race of the 2025 F1 season Piastri also signed a multi-year contract extension. His previous deal already ran until the end of 2026, and his latest agreement is likely to keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2028 -- though speculation continues to rumble on about his long-term future.

Ferrari

Lewis Hamilton - 2027

While an exact end date of Hamilton's contract -- signed after completing one of the biggest driver moves in F1 history -- was never officially communicated, Hamilton admitted earlier this year that he still had a contract in place for 2027. That means he got at least a three-year deal at Ferrari, something he had also been seeking at Mercedes.

Amid retirement rumours, Hamilton has also crushed speculation and assured fans that he wasn't going anywhere just yet.

He said: "There's a lot of people that are trying to retire me, and that's not even in my thoughts. I'm already thinking of what will be next, and planning for, like, the next five years. But I still plan to be here for some time."

Charles Leclerc - 2028

Leclerc, who first joined Ferrari in 2019, signed another multi-year extension ahead of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix.

The team did not publicly reveal an exact expiry date, but the new agreement is understood to take Leclerc to 2028 and potentially beyond, giving Ferrari long-term security over one side of its driver lineup.

Red Bull

Max Verstappen - 2030

Red Bull confirmed in 2022 that four-time world champion Verstappen would remain with the team until the end of 2028 in one of the longest deals on the F1 grid.

Sources told ESPN that performance-related clauses in Verstappen's contract could allow him to leave early, but the Dutchman has now signed a new contract extension with Red Bull until 2030 ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix.

Isack Hadjar - 2027

Isack Hadjar was promoted from Racing Bulls to partner Verstappen for the 2026 season after an impressive rookie campaign. He has now signed a contract extension with Red Bull, securing his seat for the 2027 season.

Mercedes

George Russell - beyond 2026

Russell agreed a new deal with Mercedes ahead of the 2026 season following lengthy negotiations with team principal Toto Wolff.

Although the agreement was initially confirmed as taking him through at least 2026, Russell has since described it as a multi-year deal and said he will fulfill the performance clauses in his contract to stay at Mercedes next year.

Kimi Antonelli - TBC

Mercedes' Antonelli has only been given one-year contracts since his debut, but given his form this season there's no way he'll be leaving the Silver Arrows. Right?

No official announcements have been made yet, but Antonelli could be celebrating both a maiden title and a bumper new deal this year.

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso - TBC

Alonso's current Aston Martin deal runs until the end of the 2026 season, and he said a decision on his future will come later in the year. At 45 years old, the decision is likely to be between continuing with an underperforming Aston Martin team, or calling time on his F1 career once and for all.

Lance Stroll - TBC

Stroll signed a contract extension in 2024 which kept him with Aston Martin for 2025 "and beyond," but no specific end date was announced. Part of that ambiguity, of course, is because he's the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll.

He remains with the team for 2026, although his position for 2027 has not formally been confirmed.

Alpine

Pierre Gasly - 2028

Gasly is one of the drivers whose future is already settled -- the Frenchman signed a new multi-year agreement with Alpine in 2025 which keeps him locked in at the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

Franco Colapinto - 2027

Colapinto retained his Alpine seat alongside Gasly for 2026 after taking over from Jack Doohan during the previous season. He has now signed a new contract with the team, meaning the Argentinian will continue with Alpine for the 2027 season.

Haas

Rafael Câmara - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2027

F2 star Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon for the 2027 season on a multi-year agreement. The reigning Formula 3 champion and current Formula 2 leader will make his debut in F1 and will partner fellow Ferrari Driver Academy member Oliver Bearman.

Oliver Bearman - TBC

Bearman joined Haas on a multi-year deal when he became a full-time F1 driver in 2025. The exact duration of Bearman's contract has not been made public, leaving his 2027 status uncertain for now.

However, sources with good knowledge of the team's thinking have told ESPN that Bearman is almost certain to stay with the team in 2027 unless a Ferrari seat opens up, then the Englishman remains effectively loaned to Haas.

Racing Bulls

Liam Lawson - TBC

Lawson remained with Racing Bulls for 2026 after rebuilding his season following a short-lived promotion to Red Bull the previous year.

His seat is only confirmed for the current season, meaning the New Zealander will again have to prove his case if he is to stay within the Red Bull set-up in 2027.

Arvid Lindblad - TBC

Lindblad became the latest Red Bull junior to make the jump to Formula 1 when he was handed a Racing Bulls seat for 2026.

The rookie is currently only confirmed for this season and the team have played down speculation over their driver lineup for 2027. You'd be shocked to see him go anywhere, though.

Williams

Carlos Sainz - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Sainz originally joined Williams on a deal covering the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with "options to extend" his stay beyond that. He has recently spoken about wanting to make the Williams project work, leading to him signing a new multi-year extension with the team.

Alex Albon - 2027

Albon signed a new one-year contract with Williams during the summer break, tying him down for the 2027 season. The short-term deal is interesting, given Albon's last contract -- signed in 2024 -- was for multiple years. Keeping those options open?

Audi

Nico Hulkenberg - TBC

Hulkenberg joined Sauber ahead of its transformation into the Audi team on a multi-year contract in 2025.

There are believed to be options in his deal which could allow him to remain with Audi beyond 2026, but an exact end date has not been announced.

Gabriel Bortoleto - TBC

Bortoleto joined Hulkenberg at Sauber before the team's transition to Audi and also signed a multi-year deal.

The Brazilian is contracted through at least the end of 2026, but his place for 2027 has not yet been officially confirmed.

Cadillac

Sergio Perez - 2027

Perez returned to the Formula 1 grid with Cadillac for the team's debut season in 2026 after spending a year away from racing.

The Mexican joined on a multi-year agreement understood to be on similar terms to teammate Valtteri Bottas, putting him in line to remain with Cadillac for 2027.

Valtteri Bottas - 2027

Bottas also returned to a full-time race seat with Cadillac after spending 2025 as Mercedes' reserve driver.

The Finn signed a multi-year deal which runs until at least the end of 2027, giving the new team one of the few already settled driver pairings heading into next season.

stories.headline: UFC champ Alexander Volkanovski proposes 'send-off' superbout vs. Justin Gaethje
stories.summary: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski is calling for a "send-off" superfight against lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.
stories.body:
UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski has proposed a "send-off" superfight between himself and lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Volkanovski (28-4) is scheduled to defend his 145-pound title against Movsar Evloev (20-0) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Arguably the greatest featherweight of all time, Volkanovski has acknowledged he is approaching the end of his career at 38 years old. Gaethje, 37, has acknowledged the same since he claimed the UFC's 155-pound title for the first time in June.

With both champions seemingly near the end of their time in the Octagon, Volkanovski has suggested a winner-take-all scenario in 2027.

"Imagine that, do it as a send-off," Volkanovski told the "Who Da Fook Are These Guys?" podcast. "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

Volkanovski, of Australia, has already tried to capture the lightweight title. He famously challenged then-lightweight champion Islam Makhachev twice in a 10-month span in 2023. He suffered a razor-close decision loss to Makhachev in their first meeting in February then lost by first-round knockout in an October rematch that was scheduled on short notice.

Gaethje (28-5) has not even guaranteed whether he will fight again or retire off his historic win at the White House in June, but he has stated that he believes his next challenger would be lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski appears to be throwing his name into the mix in the hope of changing those plans.

"He's said, 'What's the point of doing rematches,'" Volkanovski said. "Let's do a superfight then [retire] straight away after, let the divisions sort themselves out. The UFC would be happy for that. Let's make it happen."

stories.headline: Judge sides with NRL over NZ Rugby on Chiefs name
stories.summary: Rugby league has struck the first blow in the Chief name wars, with New Zealand Rugby's urgent injunction denied ahead of the new PNG NRL club's jersey reveal.
stories.body:
New Zealand's High Court has knocked back an application for an interim injunction on the PNG Chiefs NRL franchise using its name in the country.

New Zealand Rugby (NZR) had rushed to court ahead of the PNG team's logo and jersey reveal in Port Moresby next week.

The organisation claimed use of the Chiefs name, also the name of the long-standing Super Rugby Pacific outfit, would cause confusion and damage to the brand value.

But a judge at Friday's two-hour Wellington hearing turned down the application after hearing an injunction could harm the NRL expansion outfit's efforts to attract players ahead of a 2028 debut.

The dispute remains though, with the application for a final injunction still before the court and legal action in Australia a consideration.

ARLC executive chairman Peter V'landys last week labelled NZR's action one of "mind-blowing hypocrisy", using the example of the Auckland Blues' arrival decades after the NSW Blues "had been the Blues".

"Today's decision is not a judgement on the strength of our case, and the matter will still be heard in full," NZR boss Steve Lancaster said.

"As the trademark holder, our responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand hasn't changed. We remain open to working with the ARLC on a solution."

NZR's lawyer Earl Gray argued on Friday that the PNG Chiefs' use of 'PNG Chiefs' and 'Chiefs' interchangeably created confusion for fans of both codes and that, with no clear distinction between the two, it would strip the rugby Chiefs' brand exclusivity.

He said NZR had trademark protections for the Chiefs in New Zealand that the NRL had not acknowledged.

ARLC laywer Clive Elliot argued that the request for an urgent injunction, about a year after NZR became aware of the PNG Chiefs name, was not appropriate.

He said an injunction now would cloud the franchise's reputation ahead of a recruitment blitz once free agency opens in November.

stories.headline: Packers' Josh Jacobs eligible to return next week amid probe
stories.summary: Packers RB Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week.
stories.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list on Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week.

The league's investigation into Jacobs under the personal conduct policy remains ongoing, however, leaving open the possibility that he could still be suspended.

When he comes off the list next week, Jacobs will have missed the first six games of the season and those games would count toward any suspension. However, if Jacobs is suspended for more than six games, he would have to miss additional games.

After playing the Cowboys this Sunday at Lambeau Field, the Packers visit the Lions on Oct. 25. It's possible Jacobs could play in one or more games and then have to miss move games later on if the length of the suspension warrants.

Jacobs was placed on the commissioner exempt list on Aug. 30 while the NFL continued to gather information about the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay.

Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property.

Part of the reason the league has not closed its investigation is because it has not seen the surveillance video from Jacobs' home that was noted in the criminal report. The video showed the portion of the incident that occurred in Jacobs' garage but not from inside the house.

On Sept. 24, Brown County (Wisconsin) District Court judge Marc A. Hammer lifted a temporary seal of the records and turned the decision whether to release part or all of the records to the Hobart/Lawrence (Wis.) police department.

On Tuesday, the police department announced it would release some records but did not say whether the surveillance video was part of the documents it deemed available for public consumption. However, that release would be delayed pending appeals from the parties involved.

On Wednesday, both Jacobs and the victim in the case filed suit to block the release of evidence and have it permanently sealed.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta told Arsenal job cuts will help club 'achieve success'
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.

Chief executive Richard Garlick informed staff this week that Arsenal's workforce will be reduced across a number of departments -- although the playing and coaching staff in the men's and women's teams will be unaffected.

- Arteta defends Gyökeres after goalless start to season

- Merino lucky 'to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Forest sweating on Gibbs-White fitness vs. Arsenal

The cuts are set to impact up to 7% of the club's 871 permanent staff.

Arteta was last week rewarded with a new four-year deal, worth as much as £20 million ($27m) a season, after he oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title since 2004.

Arsenal's turnover for the 2024-25 season was a record £691m ($920m).

"First, this question is not for me," Arteta said on Friday when asked about the expected job losses in his news conference ahead of Sunday's league match against Nottingham Forest.

"It was explained to me about the exercise, and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve.

"Some decisions have to be taken to put people in the right roles, and keep investing, to achieve what we want to achieve the success that we want to create. That has been explained.

"Obviously, I am not the right person to answer to that question. That's for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that."

Arteta did not take any further questions on the topic at the request of the club.

The 44-year-old Spaniard also confirmed that the club will retake Arsenal's official squad photo following William Saliba's omission.

The France international, who last season played an integral role in the club winning the league title, was conspicuous by his absence from the picture which was released on Thursday.

He is currently sidelined with a back problem, and Arsenal said he was not available because of a "medical appointment."

"We have tried to do that picture three times already," explained Arteta on Friday. "We had to cancel it at the last minute for different reasons.

"We have some commercial obligations, and we had people that flew over because of that. We decided to do that picture at least.

"We'll have another picture with the whole family. Hopefully we can get them all together at some point. He [Saliba] knows how loved he is. He's completely fine about it."

Saliba has not played since the World Cup but there is an outside chance he could be available before the international break next month.

Martín Zubimendi is in contention to face Forest despite sustaining an ankle injury in training directly after Arsenal's win over Leeds at the Emirates Stadium last weekend. Piero Hincapié, who also suffered an ankle problem during the post-match session, will not feature.

All that offseason prognostication goes out the door with the first in-season fantasy rankings of 2026-27. As always, these blend historical performance with current trajectory. Hot starts matter, but not nearly as much as what's still to come. These are go-forward rankings, built on the fantasy points yet to be scored.

The biggest shakeup comes from Broadway. With Igor Shesterkin out for the season with a knee injury, the rankings put Dylan Garand inside the top 100. But some of the bloom came off the rose Thursday, when Garand and Spencer Martin combined to allow seven goals to the New Jersey Devils.
